peerReviewScope: See independenceDisclosure. The Codex turn-2 review file name, top-level verdict token, mustFixCount, shouldFixCount and the finding id string were surfaced by an unfiltered glob scan run to establish the register's turn-2 finding-identifier convention. No finding text, no evidence, no location and no reasoning from that file was read. The finding reported here was fully determined before that scan and is not derived from it.
discipline: Refute, not confirm. Every digest recomputed from live bytes. Every shape claim measured by parsing the frozen JSON. Every live-authority claim read from the live register.
decisionRule: CONSENT only if no MUST-FIX and no SHOULD-FIX. One MUST-FIX survives verification, so the verdict is OBJECT.
findingIdentifierScope: CLAUDE-D353-T2-MF1 is this reviewer's own turn-2 finding label, formed on the register's established Claude turn-2 pattern (CLAUDE-D303-T2-SF1, CLAUDE-D319-T2-SF1). It is not an identifier invented for any other party's unlabeled finding and it is not an observation identifier. Turn-1 MF-1, leftover-join.v31 of G21 Stage A Claude G21LJ-V31-M1, leftover-join.v29 of G21 Stage A Claude G21LJ-V29-M1, G21LJ-V29-M2, G21LJ-V29-M3 and G21LJ-V29-SF1, and observations OBS-1 through OBS-5 are recited from frozen bytes, not invented.

findings.title: The draft is a turn-2 subject that still declares itself turn 1 of 3 and recites nothing of its own turn-1 round: it never names MF-1, never records that MF-1 landed here, and never records the turn-1 verdicts, digests or subject custody.
location: docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-353.draft.md line 5: '> **Protocol:** D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3.'

Whole document: the identifier MF-1 appears nowhere. Measured by grep -n over the frozen subject for 'turn', 'MF-1', 'OBJECT' and 'CONSENT'; the only turn token in the file is line 5, and there is no MF-1, no OBJECT and no turn-1 CONSENT recital anywhere in lines 1 through 100.
findings.subjectClaim: The draft presents itself as the turn-1 subject of a fresh D-000 cycle, with no review round behind it.
findings.liveFact: This is turn 2 of 3. Turn 1 closed with Claude 2 OBJECT, 1 MUST-FIX MF-1 (docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-353.review-adversarial.claude2.json, measured sha256 8dfd56001ce404bb8ec3519c0709b1f310a7317f0cf4df506611f2445eb2aba0) and Codex CONSENT 0/0 (docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-353.review-adversarial.codex.json, measured sha256 e497c59c190cd7aebb2dc34c04d6ee9f7cec8043431fe88170b031e40ab01ff1). Both digests match the values the turn-2 dispatch cites. The frozen turn-1 review records subjectMeasuredSha256 0df0ab46db65d4360a5fc7f071c434275a074a49b127aa639d46579375a0db39, 13082 bytes, 100 lines. The subject now measures b20660b5007793c8d5793edca3ac21bfdf3f7a9482617e9bbfc63a9d0547d7ed, 13162 bytes, 100 lines. The draft was therefore revised between turns, and the substance of MF-1 was in fact landed at line 84, which now reads 'leftover-join.v31 of G21 Stage A Claude REJECT returned 5 labeled observation objects OBS-1 through OBS-5 (members id, note)'. The document records neither the round that produced that change nor the identifier under which it was required.
whyThisIsAMustFix: The draft body is what becomes the COORD entry, so line 5 would record a false fact about the entry's own adoption protocol permanently. The register's own adopted entries contradict it: D-347, D-342 and D-334 were each adopted at turn 2, and each carries 'turn 2 of 3' plus what the turn lands ('Lands SF-1'; 'Lands Claude SF-1'; 'Lands the unlabeled Codex turn-1 SHOULD-FIX').

The register requires the landed turn-1 identifier to be named in the entry, not only in the coordinator's Status line. The adopted D-347 entry body states 'This entry names D-347 Stage B turn-1 Claude identifier SF-1 as landed at turn 2', alongside 'Turn-1 Claude OBJECT 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX SF-1' with the frozen review digest, 'turn-1 Codex CONSENT 0/0' with its digest, and 'Findings of turn-1 SF-1 land at turn 2.' D-353 carries none of these for MF-1.

This is not a rule the draft is unaware of. The same document names, in the same discipline, every other landed identifier and its landing site: G21LJ-V31-M1 at leftover-join.v32 of G21, the unlabeled Codex leftover-join.v31 MUST-FIX with no id member, the unlabeled Codex leftover-join.v30 MUST-FIX, and G21LJ-V29-M1, G21LJ-V29-M2, G21LJ-V29-M3 and G21LJ-V29-SF1 at leftover-join.v30 of G21. The single identifier it omits is the one from its own review round, which is the one a later reader most needs to reconstruct why the turn-1 and turn-2 bytes differ.

The omission is load-bearing for custody, not cosmetic. Turn-1 MF-1 was raised against bytes 0df0ab46db65d4360a5fc7f071c434275a074a49b127aa639d46579375a0db39. Those bytes no longer exist: the revision was written in place over docs/coop/artifacts/coordinator-decisions.D-353.draft.md, the file is untracked in git, and no D-353 path in the tree hashes to 0df0ab46. Measured: every coordinator-decisions.D-353.* path was hashed and none matches, and git ls-files returns nothing for the draft path. The turn-2 drafts of the twelve prior turn-2 rounds took a distinct path instead (coordinator-decisions.D-<N>.turn2.draft.md), leaving the turn-1 subject retrievable; D-347's turn-1 draft still measures a74492623faf46f2963151f3321eb98d1ecd14d97bd49e466223d4fe33afccd5, exactly what its frozen turn-1 review recorded. With the turn-1 bytes gone, the entry's own recital is the only surviving record that a MUST-FIX was raised and landed, and the entry does not make it.

Because the turn-1 bytes are gone, the repair cannot simply copy the D-347 sentence 'Frozen turn-1 ... stays frozen'. The entry must state turn-1 custody truthfully rather than assert a freeze that the tree does not carry.
findings.requiredCorrection: Correct line 5 to 'D-000 new cycle, turn 2 of 3' and record the turn-1 round in the entry: name MF-1, state that its findings land at turn 2, recite turn-1 Claude 2 OBJECT 1 MUST-FIX MF-1 with digest 8dfd56001ce404bb8ec3519c0709b1f310a7317f0cf4df506611f2445eb2aba0 and turn-1 Codex CONSENT 0/0 with digest e497c59c190cd7aebb2dc34c04d6ee9f7cec8043431fe88170b031e40ab01ff1, and record turn-1 subject custody as it actually stands, naming the turn-1 digest 0df0ab46db65d4360a5fc7f071c434275a074a49b127aa639d46579375a0db39 and the fact that the turn-2 revision was written at the turn-1 path rather than claiming the turn-1 subject remains frozen. Invent no identifier while doing so.
findings.whyNotCosmetic: A false 'turn 1 of 3' and a silent MUST-FIX are two independent losses in the permanent record: the first misstates how the decision was adopted, the second erases that an adversarial finding was raised and corrected. Neither is recoverable from elsewhere once the turn-1 bytes are gone.

reviewSummary: The correction ordered at turn 1 landed cleanly and completely. Line 84 now describes the frozen leftover-join.v31 of G21 Stage A Claude return shape exactly as the bytes carry it, 5 labeled observation objects OBS-1 through OBS-5 with members id and note, and it did not over-apply to the leftover-join.v30 of G21 recital, which the bytes confirm is still 5 unlabeled strings. Everything else in the entry survives an adversarial pass: all eighteen cited digests recompute to their cited values, both Stage A return shapes match member for member, all three predecessor finding landings match the frozen reviews, the successor's own bytes agree with every leftover sentence including the D-352 truncated-body remasurement and the surviving per-D-002-platform remainder, and every live-authority claim from DR-G21 OPEN to required-now 28 to condition 2 at 5 of 32 reads back from the register unchanged. Twenty enumerated attacks were tested; nineteen are absent. One is present. The entry is a turn-2 subject that still calls itself turn 1 of 3 and says nothing about the round that produced it: MF-1 is named nowhere, the fact that it landed here is recorded nowhere, and the turn-1 verdicts, digests and subject custody are absent. The register's own turn-2 precedents are uniform against this, and the omission bites harder than usual because the turn-1 bytes were overwritten in place and no longer exist, leaving the entry as the only possible record that an adversarial finding was raised and corrected. One MUST-FIX, no SHOULD-FIX. OBJECT.
